paper.title: WebGPT: Browser-assisted question-answering with human feedback
paper.central_claim: Fine-tuning GPT-3 to search and navigate a text-based web browser, collect references, and optimize human answer preferences yields human-competitive long-form QA: best BC plus reward-model rejection sampling is preferred56% to same-browser human demonstrators and69% to highest-voted ELI5 answers; references facilitate factual evaluation and TruthfulQA improves versus GPT-3 but remains below humans.

provenance.actual_model_source: Environment explicitly reports gpt-6.1-sol; no model probing performed.
provenance.rubric_caveat: Supplied SCORE_SPEC remains draft_uncalibrated. Controller directs parallel calibration/production with these hash-bound weights; any changed anchors require affected papers to be reviewed under a new version.

provenance.local_contract_check_note: Open-attempt final check normalized documented expectation enums, completed required semantic field names, made condition statuses explicit and corrected historical attribution. No score/rating changed; all replacements are atomic and restricted to this seat attempt.

evidence.quote: This model’s answers are preferred by humans 56% of the time to those of our human demonstrators, and 69% of the time to the highest-voted answer from Reddit.
evidence.support_explanation: Central reported preference comparisons, not universal truth or executable GUI completion rates.

evidence.quote: This process is then repeated with a fresh context (hence, the only memory of previous steps is what is recorded in the summary).
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit within-episode state summary; not durable experience memory.

evidence.quote: as long as there is at least one reference, the model is prompted with the question and the references, and must compose its final answer.
evidence.support_explanation: Quote-gated transition from browsing to answer synthesis.

evidence.quote: the reward represents an Elo score, scaled such that the difference between two scores represents the logit of the probability that one will be preferred to the other by the human labelers.
evidence.support_explanation: Human-preference scalar, not binary task-success or factual-truth judge.

evidence.quote: we took the reward model score at the end of each episode, and added this to a KL penalty from the BC model at each token to mitigate overoptimization of the reward model.
evidence.support_explanation: PPO reward and regularization source.

evidence.quote: We sampled a fixed number of answers (4, 16 or 64) from either the BC model or the RL model (if left unspecified, we used the BC model), and selected the one that was ranked highest by the reward model.
evidence.support_explanation: Whole-answer candidate generation and direct reward ranking without simulated next-state prediction.

evidence.quote: We used mutually disjoint sets of questions for each of BC, RM and RL.
evidence.support_explanation: Reported question separation, not proof of held-out websites or pretraining decontamination.

evidence.quote: Our final reward models were trained on around 16,000 comparisons, the remaining 5,500 being used for evaluation only.
evidence.support_explanation: RM training/evaluation counts; not the denominator of the headline ELI5 test preferences.

evidence.quote: at the end of each episode we inserted 15 additional answering-only episodes using the same references as the previous episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Training-only sample-efficiency reuse, not persistent cross-task memory.

evidence.quote: We excluded RL for simplicity, since it did not provide significant benefit when combined with rejection sampling
evidence.support_explanation: Best main models are BC plus best-of-N; do not attribute headline result to PPO.

evidence.quote: We evaluated all WebGPT models using a sampling temperature of 0.8, which was tuned using human evaluations, and with a maximum number of browsing actions of 100.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation budget and human-assisted hyperparameter selection.

evidence.quote: we stripped all citations and references from the model-generated answers, hired new contractors who were not familiar with our detailed instructions, and gave them a much more minimal set of instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Reddit comparison attempts to reduce citation/style/instruction confounds; not perfect blinding.

evidence.quote: Error bars represent ± 1 \pm 1 standard error.
evidence.support_explanation: Intervals explicitly reported in captions; numerical bars not inferred from absent image values.

evidence.quote: For WebGPT, we used human evaluation, since WebGPT’s answers are out-of-distribution for the automated metric.
evidence.support_explanation: Avoids inappropriate automatic truth judge on shifted answer style.

evidence.quote: This affected 74 answers in total, around 3% of answers.
evidence.support_explanation: Truncation produced empty answers scored true but uninformative; different denominator from ELI5 preferences.

evidence.quote: Rejection sampling provides a substantial benefit, with the 175B best-of-64 BC model being preferred 68% of the time to the 175B BC model. Meanwhile, RL provides a smaller benefit, with the 175B RL model being preferred 58% of the time to the 175B BC model.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched-base training/selection comparisons; extra inference compute remains a real causal factor.

evidence.quote: This alone closed much of the gap we originally saw between BC and RL.
evidence.support_explanation: Tuning BC epochs and temperature is a load-bearing baseline control.

evidence.quote: we used the score of a 175B “validation” reward model (trained on a separate dataset split) for these experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Scaling curves use a held-out same-family proxy rather than independent human truth labels.

evidence.quote: the 760M best-of-4 model, the 13B best-of-16 model, and the 175B best-of-64 model.
evidence.support_explanation: Compute-efficient frontier combines size and N; headline size comparison does not hold N fixed.

evidence.quote: We did not test this hypothesis directly, since we found that it was challenging for labelers to spot subtle hallucinations.
evidence.support_explanation: Lower non-imitative hallucination is explicitly a hypothesis, not directly established.

evidence.quote: the only interactions with the outside world allowed by the environment are sending queries to the Bing API and following links that already exist on the web
evidence.support_explanation: Read-only text-browser boundary: no forms or general GUI modification, but stateful page navigation is present.

evidence.quote: fetches the HTML of the web page and simplifies it using Mozilla’s Readability.js
evidence.support_explanation: Hand-engineered textual observation privilege and lossy page reduction.

evidence.quote: the link ID is the index of the link on the page, which is also used for the link-clicking command.
evidence.support_explanation: Stable action target representation within current serialized page; not coordinate grounding.

evidence.quote: We censor any pages that contain a 10-gram overlap with the question (or reference answer, if provided) to prevent the model from cheating
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit live-retrieval copying control, not exhaustive contamination audit.
Collected demonstration/comparison denominators; distinct from 19,578 released comparisons and test denominators.

evidence.quote: we measured a final researcher-labeler agreement rate of 74%, and a labeler-labeler agreement rate of 73%.
evidence.support_explanation: Label quality audit with neutral/non-neutral counted half; not model precision/NPV.

evidence.quote: we asked contractors to judge whether claims in the answer are supported , i.e., either backed up by a reliable reference, or common knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Support judgment differs from independent factual research.

evidence.quote: we outsource document retrieval to the Microsoft Bing Web Search API
evidence.support_explanation: Author explicitly inherits retrieval and focuses on faithful training objectives instead of a new search engine.

evidence.quote: This was previously suggested by Metzler et al. (2021)
evidence.support_explanation: Author-attributed predecessor of reference-assisted evaluation; original not supplied.

evidence.quote: Our model’s answers are true 75% of the time, and are both true and informative 54% of the time
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit headline TruthfulQA proportions; distinct from ELI5 preference and empty-answer counts.

scope.reason: Peripheral read-only web-interface agent: despite Bing API retrieval, policy observes page/cursor state and issues sequential link, find, scroll, back and quote actions. Not pure API orchestration, not screenshot GUI grounding and not arbitrary form/editing automation.
scope.boundary: Only search queries and following existing links affect outside world; QA is the end task.

signatures.object: Structured web navigation and evidence-conditioned answer generation
signatures.information: Question,current simplified page at cursor,indexed links,quotes,past-action summary,remaining cap; no pixels or hidden page semantics. Bing/Readability provide privileges.
signatures.operation: Serialize page/browser state to text; GPT-3 emits command; runtime fetches/scrolls/finds/quotes; refresh prompt; synthesize from question plus quotes after stop.
signatures.output: A real browsing trajectory and reference-bearing answer.
signatures.conditions: Restricted read-only actions; at least one reference for answering; invalid commands consume cap;100evaluation actions and reference cap.
signatures.feedback: Real fetched page text/errors and human command demonstrations during BC.
signatures.selection_rule: Policy token sampling selects actions; quote command must match page text; stop on explicit End/caps.
signatures.selection_data: Real fetched page text/errors and human command demonstrations during BC.
signatures.persistence: Quotes and summary stored for current episode; learned BC weights retained across tasks.
signatures.later_use: Answer phase consumes episode quotes; subsequent questions reuse weights, not a retrieved memory bank.
signatures.claimed_effect: Make external information available to a pretrained LM and make output support inspectable.
signatures.failure_boundary: Readability/alttext discard visual information; source credibility and synthesis remain fallible; no autonomous retained-improvement cycle.

signatures.information: Question, each complete candidate answer with its collected references; learned preference RM, no oracle factual outcome.
signatures.operation: Generate N independent browsing-and-answer episodes, score each terminal answer/reference bundle, submit argmax.
signatures.conditions: BC main models760M/13B/175B paired with N4/16/64; real browsing, not state simulation; read-only environment allows independent runs.
signatures.feedback: RM trained from human pairwise overall usefulness labels; final human comparisons assess selected answers.
signatures.selection_rule: Argmax scalar RM score over full candidate answer bundles; ranking not binary success verification.
signatures.selection_data: RM trained from human pairwise overall usefulness labels; final human comparisons assess selected answers.
signatures.persistence: Selected answer retained for current output only; ranking does not update policy or create reusable skills.
signatures.later_use: End user receives selected answer; future questions start fresh with fixed policy/RM.
signatures.failure_boundary: Compute grows with whole-rollout candidates, possible shared-RM overoptimization/cherry-picking; no matched random-N/alternative judge causal arm.

signatures.information: 6209human demos,21548collected comparisons; RM inputquestion/answer/references; disjoint BC/RM/RLquestion sets; no true task-success oracle.
signatures.operation: BC action-token imitation; train pairwise Elo RM; optionally PPO terminal RM plus per-token KL; reuse15answer-only episodes per browsing episode.
signatures.output: Static fine-tuned policy and preference scorer; main chosen systemBC+bestN rather thanRL.
signatures.conditions: Three GPT-3 sizes; RM16Ktrain/5.5Keval comparisons, held-outBCvalidation and early stopping; live retrieval in training.
signatures.feedback: Human supported-useful/coherent preference; additional PPO samples obtain RM scores.
signatures.selection_rule: Validation accuracy/RMscore plus human tuning select stopping/temperature; fixed weights deployed.
signatures.selection_data: Human supported-useful/coherent preference; additional PPO samples obtain RM scores.
signatures.persistence: Saved trained model parameters; not accepted autonomous modifications selected on later independent tasks.
signatures.later_use: Weights serve subsequent questions; same-episode quote reuse is training efficiency only.
signatures.claimed_effect: RL58%preference versusBC, less than bestN gain; added answer episodes about2×sample efficiency according to authors.
signatures.failure_boundary: Preference/support proxy can be biased and hacked, citations can induce overreliance, independent truth not guaranteed.

gap.author_gap: LFQA retrieval/synthesis exist but ordinary language modeling and overlap metrics do not directly optimize supported useful answer quality or faithfully evaluate factual claims.
gap.checked_gap: Paper documents mismatch of ROUGE-like metrics and subjective truth evaluation; interactive evidence acquisition plus reference-assisted human preferences is a concrete contemporary response. Does not prove first-ever browsing, RLHF, retrieval QA or citations.

tactic_steps_checked: Manufacture text substrate from structured browser states, page links, PDF/HTML text and commands.
Use one GPT-3 next-token policy for browse commands and answer text, with human command demonstrations.
The interface artifact changes access to external evidence; it is not merely concatenating another natural-language prompt.

success_failure_checks.reason: C18 serialization operation and parent heterogeneous-to-shared-text definition are present.
No independent semantic-interface probe or controlled remove-serializer/backbone-matched ablation; success conditions not fully met.
Readability and alt-text discard visual/layout information; no universal multimodal capability.
Three scales of one GPT-3 family, not architecture-family transfer; human-preference RM objective is a separate head and prevents a fully uniform-objective claim.

matches.reason: Partial C18 is a concrete structured-web-to-text serializer enabling pretrained next-token control. It does not establish that unification itself caused gains; RLHF and best-of-N are not automatically self-supervised signal engineering or differentiable design search.

rs_pattern.reason: C18 partial captures manufactured text substrate, not all RLHF/ranking machinery. Original15+31 overviews and full parent/child consulted before GUI mapping.
rs_pattern.executes_pattern: Serializes heterogeneous web/document/browser state into one next-token policy interface.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: Only partial: feasible browser QA and preference gains, no controlled demonstration that the serializer alone closes the gap.

condition_checks.reason: Whole-run candidates and separately trained human-preference scorer implement direct reranking.
No simulation: per-candidate quotes/answer preserved; final-state GUI success is not being checked.
N and compute frontier stated, no full latency or equal-cost scorer control.
Terminal graded score is used for PPO/ranking.
Input answer/reference bundle and human-preference target differ from GUI-success screenshot verdict; do not claim binary verifier reliability.
Held-out comparison evaluation and human audits present; no unseen-agent success precision/NPV.
SimplifiedHTML/PDF/text and indexed link targets explicitly replace screen pixels.
Observation privileges and loss of layout/images are stated; not equivalent to pixel-grounding skill.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Serializer manufactures dominant text substrate; indexed links simultaneously define observation and action grounding.
pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: RS general cross-substrate tactic versus GUI-specific text/DOM observation. Text-browser serialization is real but lacks isolation ablation; no one-to-one taxonomy equivalence.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_differences: RS general cross-substrate tactic versus GUI-specific text/DOM observation. Text-browser serialization is real but lacks isolation ablation; no one-to-one taxonomy equivalence.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: Full-answer RM argmax reranking is an additional GUI mechanism, not forced into an originalRSclass.
pattern_mapping.conditions_and_differences: Human preference RM and real independent browsing; no learned dynamics or correctness guarantee.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_differences: Human preference RM and real independent browsing; no learned dynamics or correctness guarantee.
